blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Account deletion keeps the member's e-mail, name, phone and postal address) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: "UPDATE users SET deleted_at = datetime('now'), password_hash = NULL WHERE id = ?",
findings.recommendation: The proposal promises that the button "erases the member's personal data" and that orders are kept "without personal data", but delete_account only sets deleted_at and clears password_hash: after a deletion, the users row still holds email, display_name, phone and postal_address (app/schema.sql:3-6), and every orders row still points at it through orders.user_id, so the kept orders remain linked to the member's identity. This breaks the right to erasure (GDPR Art. 17) and storage limitation (Art. 5(1)(e)). Overwrite the personal columns in the same UPDATE — phone and postal_address to NULL, display_name to a neutral value, email to a unique non-personal placeholder such as 'deleted-<id>' since the column is NOT NULL UNIQUE — keeping the row only as the anonymous anchor of the orders; and add a test that reads the row back after delete_account and asserts no personal column is left (the current tests only check sign-in and sessions).
findings.title: Account deletion keeps the member's e-mail, name, phone and postal address

findings.evidence:
def delete_account(user_id: int) -> None:
    """Deletes the member's account; their orders are kept for accounting."""
findings.recommendation: The change keeps the users row of a deleted member indefinitely (soft delete) and says nothing about how long it stays, nor about the copies of the erased data in database backups of members.db. State the retention of the soft-deleted row and of backups (how long until the erasure reaches them, or how a restore re-applies past deletions), per GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) and Art. 17. Recorded with low confidence: the backup setup is not visible in the repository.
findings.title: No retention or purge rule for deleted accounts, backups included

findings.recommendation: analytics_id is new in this change but nothing in the change or the repository calls it, and the proposal does not mention analytics: either drop it from this change or state its purpose (data minimisation, GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)). It is a pseudonymous identifier, still personal data: with a fixed salt and a kept users row, events keyed by it stay linkable to the member after delete_account, which neither deletes those events nor breaks the link. If analytics events are kept, make erasure reach them (delete the member's events, or derive the id from a per-user random value erased at deletion). Recorded with low confidence: the analytics store and its callers are not visible in the repository.
findings.title: analytics_id is added with no use, and deletion does not reach the events it keys
